static_traits.name: Han Rui
static_traits.occupation: College freshman, member of the school track team
static_traits.social_status: relationships with roommates and teammates affected by self-criticism and guilt, often choosing self-isolation; has a few friends and teammates to talk with, but has not yet discussed these specific thoughts
static_traits.medical_history: no history of similar problems; never received psychological counseling;No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: clear expression, fairly good logic, highly cooperative,Positive attitude; speech rate Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: diet-related guilt and self-criticism (especially eating pizza). Triggered and gradually worsened by academic and training pressure since joining the university track team this semester, appearing almost daily, especially After training or on 'cheat day'. Tried coping by restricting diet and increasing exercise but negative thoughts not yet eased.
basic_info.core_demands: seeking support to cope with these unhealthy thought patterns, easing Self-blame and guilt, improving self-esteem and overall well-being.
growth_experiences: entering university as a freshman and joining the school track team, needing to balance academics and training; thus associating foods like pizza with 'lack of discipline/affecting performance', with frequent Intense guilt and self-criticism after eating (almost daily, more obvious After training or on 'cheat day'); tried compensating with strict diet restriction and more exercise, but negative thinking has not yet improved.

core_beliefs: only by maintaining perfect discipline and control am I valuable/qualified (especially as an Athlete).
eating 'indulgent' foods like pizza means I have failed, unworthy of being a qualified Athlete.

special_situations.event: After training ends or on a 'cheat day', eats pizza with classmates
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: as an Athlete must always be strictly disciplined, eating only 'healthy' foods; relaxing the diet will affect performance and progress
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strictly restricts diet and increases exercise to compensate; maintains 'discipline' through self-reproach
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not eat this;I will ruin all progress.

special_situations.event: When thinking about or planning to eat pizza
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: one 'unhealthy' meal will ruin all previous training and nutrition management
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Undoing 'losses' through extra training and stricter diet control

special_situations.event: recalling one's choices and identity (as an Athlete) after eating pizza
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: either fully disciplined or a failure; no gray areas or moderate enjoyment allowed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reinforcing absolutist standards with rule-based self-Demands like 'should/must', avoiding relaxing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: eating pizza once shows I lack discipline/I am a failed Athlete.

special_situations.event: Thinking about confiding these thoughts to friends or teammates
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: expressing troubles will be seen as weakness or troubling others; others will not understand me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Chooses silence and self-isolation, avoids discussing with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: they will not understand, I should not trouble others.

core_conflict.wish: longing to be recognized as a qualified Athlete while freely enjoying food and life without blame
core_conflict.fear: fear that relaxing will lead to failure, being judged or rejected, losing value and belonging
defense_goal: Maintains safety and control through self-reproach and strict self-discipline
avoiding expressing needs and seeking help to dodge Being rejected/being misunderstood
Repressing hedonistic urges with high standards to reduce shame and anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: an Athlete/Student not disciplined enough, needing perfect performance to prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: harsh judges (teammates, roommates or others), people who will not understand and may be disappointed

object_relations.self_representation: A burden who may trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: Others who would be dragged down by me or forced to comfort me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked or thinking about discussing diet-related distress and emotions with friends/teammates
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: expressing will burden others and gain no understanding (transference: seeing others as judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expresses in a tone of self-blame and lowered self-worth, avoiding raising concrete requests or seeking help, downplaying her own needs in her words.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: when value judgments like 'Athlete diet discipline/whether eating pizza is allowed' come up
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries emotional expression will be seen as weakness, so emphasizes rules and rational standards instead
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: using rule-based and abstract expressions (e.g. 'should/must'), restrained tone, avoiding emotional words and subjective feelings.

manifestations: constraining self-choices with external 'should/must' standards, believing Athletes cannot eat pizza
Lacks flexibility in eating; fears relaxing self-control
outcomes: Interference with daily life (sleep, training rhythm)

manifestations: worrying 'they will not understand', avoiding communication with friends and teammates
outcomes: Insufficient use of the support system

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: frequently using 'should/must' phrasing (e.g. 'as an Athlete I should be more disciplined')
treating 'eating pizza = lack of discipline/failure' as a hard standard for oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: often saying 'I should not trouble others', turning the urge to express and seek help back onto oneself
When emotionally distressed, chooses self-isolation rather than seeking support

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: assuming others will not understand or will be dragged down, thus not communicating
Attributes potential evaluation and blame to others' perspective to avoid self-expression

exception_events.target_problem: after eating pizza or on 'cheat day', the client usually feels Strong guilt and believes training and nutrition progress will be ruined, then blames oneself and Avoids socializing.
exception_events.unique_outcome: the client noticed performance does not worsen every time after eating pizza; in these cases the feared 'performance decline' did not appear, and the Sense of guilt was more controllable than Anticipated.
exception_events.reason: clues: observed objective performance does not always match worries; actual training state, rest and overall diet structure may buffer, weakening the belief that 'one indulgence = total loss'.

positive_force: Willing to seek professional help, positive attitude
having self-Reflection and cognitive restructuring ability (able to propose alternative thoughts like 'this meal will not define my progress')
Has certain social support resources (friends and teammates)
Strong sense of purpose and self-discipline (continuously participates in learning and training)
negative_force: harsh self-blame, with stress Turning against the self
Worries about being misunderstood and avoids communication, leading to social isolation
Uses dietary restriction and excessive exercise as a fixed compensatory strategy, maintaining the negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: After eating foods such as pizza, strong guilt and self-criticism appear
antecedent: When academic and athletic pressure is high
target_behavior.core_reason: the Introjected standard of 'as an Athlete must be absolutely disciplined' and overgeneralized cognition that 'one indulgence will ruin progress'
target_behavior.function: temporarily easing anxiety about failure and loss of control through self-blame and Reinforced control (escaping unwelcome emotions)
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, sleep and exercise rhythms affected,Declining academic performance

antecedent: When thinking about talking to friends or teammates about these thoughts
target_behavior.core_reason: mentalizing inference (mind-reading) of worrying others will not understand and fearing being a burden
target_behavior.function: escaping the discomfort of potential judgment or Being rejected, reducing immediate anxiety through isolation
